subject: Exec update: selector v2 canary regression (mitigated) + reattempt plan
body:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Kim <grace.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:44 AM
Subject: Exec update: selector v2 canary regression (mitigated) + reattempt plan

Mateo — quick heads-up on the selector v2 canary.

Summary:
- We saw a p95 latency regression in us-east canary cohort shortly after enabling selector v2 at 5% on Hosted.
- Mitigation was immediate rollback (feature flag) to selector v1 for the cohort. We’re currently stable.

What happened (high level):
- Regression concentrated on A10 long-context prompts (prefill-heavy). Early read: kernel choice in long-context bucket on A10 is suboptimal; selection telemetry points to a single kernel_id dominating that bucket.
- No correctness issues observed in canary (no NaN alerts, no conformance failures triggered).

Impact:
- Duration: ~18 minutes from enable to rollback.
- Scope: canary cohort only (5% traffic in us-east). No SLA breach; we did see elevated tail latency for affected GPU SKU bucket.

What we did:
- Rolled back to v1 via kill switch (no deploy required).
- Preserved traces + selector telemetry for analysis.
- SRE guardrails held; alert fired appropriately.

Plan / next steps:
1) Runtime to identify exact A10 long-context mapping issue (Grace/Yuki/Hiro already on it).
2) Patch + rerun benchmark sweep on A10 long-context distribution; update registry entry if needed.
3) Reattempt canary at 1% (instead of 5%) with tightened monitors + 30 min soak.

I’ll send another update after we have a concrete fix + benchmark confirmation.

— Ava
Ava Chen
VP, Platform & Reliability
Redwood Inference


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Kim <grace.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Exec update: selector v2 canary regression (mitigated) + reattempt plan

Thanks Ava.

Confirming from Release Eng side:
- Kill switch rollback completed at 09:31 PT (config propagated across us-east). No runtime version change.
- We’ve paused the rollout checklist (ENG-3934) at “Stage 1: 5% Hosted us-east” pending fix + sign-off.

Ask for Runtime/SRE: please reply here with (a) the suspected root cause and (b) explicit acceptance threshold for the reattempt (e.g., p95 within +2% per GPU bucket, plus overall error rate steady).

Connor


From: Grace Kim <grace.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:37 AM
Subject: Re: Exec update: selector v2 canary regression (mitigated) + reattempt plan

Initial root cause hypothesis (still validating):

- The scheduler-provided seq-length bucket boundary appears to be off-by-one at the upper edge of the “8k–16k prefill” bucket. That misclassifies some 16k-ish prompts into the next bucket, which selects a kernel tuned for a different prefill regime on A10.
- Telemetry: the regressed traffic shows selector_version=v2, gpu_sku=A10, seq_bucket=prefill_16k_plus picking kernel_id=attn_prefill_v7_a10 (name in registry) with a sharp p95 increase.

Mitigation / fix path:
- We already have a candidate patch in review to correct the bucket boundary logic (ties to the scheduler signal) and will update the A10 long-context entry in the registry if needed.

Reattempt proposal:
- Gate reattempt on perf-canary run on A10 long-context distribution showing:
  - p95 <= +2% vs v1 for (A10, long prefill buckets)
  - overall p95 <= +1% us-east Hosted baseline
  - no increase in NaN/correctness counters; conformance tests green

If we can land the fix today, we can rerun the benchmark sweep tonight and reattempt at 1% tomorrow morning.

Grace


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Kim <grace.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:26 AM
Subject: Re: Exec update: selector v2 canary regression (mitigated) + reattempt plan

Good rollback execution and quick triage.

Let’s do the reattempt exactly as proposed:
- 1% canary, 30 min soak minimum, with explicit A10 long-context panels in view.
- Ship only after: perf-canary gate passes + Allison/Aisha sign off on monitors.

Ava — please send me the before/after numbers once the benchmark rerun is done, even if it’s a small win. The key is “no surprises” across SKUs.

Mateo

Mateo Alvarez
VP Engineering, Runtime
Redwood Inference
